summary: U.S. fighter jets struck an IRGC missile launch site on Iran's Qeshm Island in a self-defense operation, marking a direct military confrontation. Israel maintains high alert for a potential attack on Iran but requires U.S. coordination per the Chief of Staff. Houthi drones reportedly targeted two Saudi oil pumping stations west of Riyadh.
key_points: U.S. Central Command confirmed precision strikes on an IRGC missile launch site on Qeshm Island in response to threats against U.S. forces. (Source: @yediotnews25/138069)
Israeli Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir insists U.S. coordination is a prerequisite for any strike on Iran, while PM Netanyahu and Defense Minister maintain alert directives. (Source: @yediotnews25/138067)
Houthi forces claim five drones attacked two oil pumping stations on the East-West pipeline west of Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. (Source: @yediotnews25/138061)
IDF and police thwarted a Kalashnikov rifle smuggling attempt via balloons from Egypt into the Nitzana border area. (Source: @N12chat/235578)
Mossad reportedly thwarted an Iranian attack in Greece and warned Israeli businessmen to take precautions. (Source: @N12chat/235585)
Iraqi Kataib Hezbollah vows to remain in Jurf al-Sakhr despite government pressure, warning of sectarian conflict. (Source: @Faytuks_Network/10185)
IRGC Quds Force commander Qaani visited Baghdad to negotiate Jurf al-Sakhar control, while Kataib Hezbollah offered pipeline control to Energy Police. (Source: @shin_persian/12490)
Two U.S. aircraft carriers, USS Theodore Roosevelt and USS George Washington, are operating together in the Arabian Sea. (Source: @Faytuks_Network/10186)

sections.executive_summary: U.S. forces conducted precision strikes on an Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps missile launch site on Qeshm Island, Iran, in a self-defense operation confirmed by CENTCOM. Israel's military leadership maintains readiness for potential strikes on Iran but emphasizes mandatory coordination with Washington, while the Prime Minister and Defense Minister have not altered alert directives. Meanwhile, Houthi militants claim responsibility for drone attacks on two Saudi oil pumping stations west of Riyadh, escalating Red Sea energy infrastructure threats.

points: U.S. fighter jets attacked an IRGC missile launch site on Qeshm Island using precision munitions in a self-defense operation, according to a senior U.S. military official; CENTCOM remains on high alert to protect U.S. personnel and assets in the region. (Source: @yediotnews25/138069)

Iranian media reported additional explosions on Qeshm Island following the U.S. strike, citing the deputy governor of Hormozgan Province for political, security, and social affairs, Nafisi. (Source: @Faytuks_Network/10175)

A missile launch was detected from Omidiyeh in Khuzestan Province heading south at 1521Z, and UAV activity was observed at Mount Soffeh in Isfahan at 1813Z, indicating heightened Iranian air defense or offensive readiness. (Source: @shin_persian/12486, @shin_persian/12497)
Another missile was launched from Qorveh in Kurdistan Province at 1829Z, further suggesting dispersed missile activity across western and southwestern Iran. (Source: @shin_persian/12496)

Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu and Defense Minister have not changed the IDF's alert directive for a potential attack on Iran, but Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir insists tight coordination with the U.S. military is a prerequisite for any such operation. (Source: @yediotnews25/138067)

IDF and Israel Police thwarted an overnight attempt to smuggle Kalashnikov rifles into Israel from Egypt using balloons in the Nitzana border area; the weapons were transferred to police for investigation. (Source: @N12chat/235578, @manniefabian/59541)
Mossad reportedly assisted in thwarting an Iranian-planned attack in Greece and issued advance warnings to Israeli businessmen to take security precautions. (Source: @N12chat/235585)

An Israeli Air Force GLF5 Nachshon Eitam electronic reconnaissance aircraft conducted SIGINT collection over Palestine at 21,625 feet, identified by callsign IRON and squawk 1546. (Source: @redlinkleb/53638)

Foreign Minister Gideon Saar rejected British sanctions on Israeli companies, declaring Israel will not yield and will implement countermeasures, including exploring ways to strengthen settlements in Judea and Samaria. (Source: @yediotnews25/138056, @amitsegal/67310)

Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir emphasized that U.S. coordination is essential for any Israeli strike on Iran, though he does not oppose such action; the Prime Minister and Defense Minister have maintained existing alert directives. (Source: @yediotnews25/138067)

Israeli electronic reconnaissance aircraft conducted signals intelligence collection over Palestinian territory, indicating ongoing surveillance operations in the Gaza-West Bank theater. (Source: @redlinkleb/53638)
Lebanese media reported Israeli artillery fire targeting the Wadi Zibqin area in southern Lebanon, marking continued cross-border shelling. (Source: @yediotnews25/138062)
The Lebanese Army conducted a controlled explosion in the town of Tir Dibba between 12:00 and 13:00 local time, per local monitoring channels. (Source: @redlinkleb/53589)

Iraqi Kataib Hezbollah spokesperson declared the group will not withdraw from Jurf al-Sakhr despite government pressure, warning of a national crisis and sectarian conflict, and accusing the Prime Minister of adventurism. (Source: @Faytuks_Network/10185)

IRGC Quds Force commander Esmail Qaani visited Baghdad to negotiate a Jurf al-Sakhar arrangement with Iraqi Prime Minister Al-Zaidi, though reports differ on whether the meeting occurred; Kataib Hezbollah simultaneously offered to transfer pipeline control to the Energy Police while vowing to retain control of Jurf al-Sakhr. (Source: @shin_persian/12490)

Houthi militants claimed responsibility for launching five drones that struck two oil pumping stations on the East-West pipeline west of Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, threatening energy infrastructure. (Source: @yediotnews25/138061)

The U.S. Navy deployed two aircraft carrier strike groups, USS Theodore Roosevelt (CVN 71) and USS George Washington (CVN 73), operating together in the Arabian Sea as of November 17, per CENTCOM confirmation. (Source: @Faytuks_Network/10186)

sections.threat_assessment: The direct U.S. strike on an IRGC missile site in Iran marks a significant escalation in U.S.-Iran confrontation, likely prompting Iranian retaliatory calculus through proxies. Israel's insistence on U.S. coordination for any Iran strike creates a strategic dependency that may delay or shape Israeli action. Houthi drone attacks on Saudi oil infrastructure demonstrate persistent Red Sea energy threats despite international naval presence. Iraqi militia defiance in Jurf al-Sakhr risks intra-Shia conflict and complicates Baghdad's security control. Iranian missile launches from multiple provinces suggest heightened readiness or signaling.
sections.regional_response: Saudi Arabia faces renewed Houthi pressure on critical oil infrastructure, potentially drawing deeper U.S. defensive involvement. Iraq's government
